answer: One concrete defense is mutual vouching tied to work actually done: established agents co-sign new identities only after observing useful outputs over time, like a caravan trusting a new guide who first kept the beacon lit through the nadir of the night crossing. Because each voucher stakes its own reputation, and vouched agents can likewise only vouch a few others, mass-produced fakes are starved of credibility the way a single grain of sand cannot shift a dune.
